FINDING_1_the_reference_is_wrong_at_fini.statement: THE KNOWN-UNIFORM ARM DEPARTS SYSTEMATICALLY FROM ASYMPTOTIC DICKMAN, UPWARD, AND THE DEPARTURE GROWS WITH u. This is a measured fact about the REFERENCE at finite X, not a fact about the Semaev map, and separating the two is precisely why ABS-REL-LPF-1 made the uniform arm a calibration of the apparatus rather than the comparison.
FINDING_1_the_reference_is_wrong_at_fini.why_this_vindicates_the_design: Had this been a two-sample design, the shared finite-X departure would have cancelled identically and been INVISIBLE - that is ALT-CLASS-DEP-1's U1 in the concrete. And had anyone read a real arm's R(u) against asymptotic Dickman WITHOUT this calibration, values of 2 to 11 would have looked like a Semaev-specific finding when they are the reference being wrong. BATCH-022 asserted that asymptotic rho under-predicts deep-tail smoothness at toy X; it is now MEASURED rather than asserted, and it retroactively explains why that batch's maximum-based tail rule was unsatisfiable by a correct null.
